registerNotMeasured: Not measured. This file is a cognate record, not a register pass: there is no scripts/l10n/detectors/de.js and nothing here measured the formal/informal register of the de bundle, so selfcheck must not report a register verdict for de.
scopeNote: COGNATE RECORD for de. Every value in l10n/de.json that was byte-identical to the English source has been reviewed one by one: each is either recorded below with a written reason, or was replaced by a real translation in the same pass. The list is therefore closed - a NEW identical value in de means a new judgement, not an existing licence.

cognates.3: Numeric literal; identical in every locale.
cognates.30: Numeric literal; identical in every locale.
cognates.App: German uses 'die App'; Nextcloud core de renders it identically.
cognates.Avatar: International term, spelled and used identically in German.
cognates.Branch: Git branch; German developer usage keeps 'Branch' (core de does too).
cognates.Chunk: Text-splitting term; German technical writing keeps 'Chunk'.
cognates.Chunks: Same loan; the German plural is also 'Chunks'.
cognates.Code: Same spelling and meaning in German (der Code).
cognates.Compliance: Established loan in German governance language; 'Compliance' is the standard term.
cognates.ConfigSet: Apache SOLR's own object name; used untranslated in German SOLR documentation.
cognates.ConfigSet:: Apache SOLR's object name plus a colon; nothing translatable.
cognates.DSAR: Acronym (Data Subject Access Request); used untranslated in German privacy practice.
cognates.Dashboard: Established English loan in German UI language; core de keeps it untranslated.
cognates.Deck: Nextcloud app name; kept untranslated in every finished locale.
cognates.Excel (.xlsx): Product name plus a file extension; nothing translatable.
cognates.Flows: The app's own feature name, deliberately kept in English in nl, de and da.
cognates.Format: Same spelling and meaning in German (das Format).
cognates.Handler: Established loan; the standard German term for an event/delivery handler.
cognates.Host: 'Host' is the German technical term too.
cognates.Host *: 'Host' is the German technical term; the asterisk is a required-field marker.
cognates.IBANs: Acronym; the German plural is written 'IBANs'.
cognates.ID:: Acronym plus a colon; German puts no space before a colon.
cognates.Id: The same acronym in the casing the source uses.
cognates.Index: Same spelling and meaning in German (der Index).
cognates.Label: Established loan, standard in German UI language.
cognates.Labels: Same loan; the German plural is also 'Labels'.
cognates.Linear: Same spelling in German as a standalone option label.
cognates.Links: German uses 'Link'; the plural is also 'Links'.
cognates.Mappings: This bundle already writes 'Eingabe-Mapping' / 'Ausgabe-Mapping'; the plural is 'Mappings'.
cognates.Maximum: Same spelling and meaning in German (das Maximum).
cognates.Minimum: Same spelling and meaning in German (das Minimum).
cognates.N/A: Not-applicable abbreviation, kept as-is in every locale of this app.
cognates.Name: Same spelling and meaning in German (der Name).
cognates.Name *: Same word; the asterisk is a required-field marker.
cognates.Name*: Same word; the asterisk is a required-field marker (no space in the source).
cognates.OpenCorporates: Name of an external data source; a proper noun.
cognates.OpenDocument (.ods): Format name plus a file extension; nothing translatable.
cognates.OpenRegister: The application's own name; a proper noun.
cognates.Organisation: Same spelling in German with this (non-Swiss) orthography.
cognates.Parallel:: Same spelling in German plus a colon.
cognates.Person: Same spelling and meaning in German (die Person).
cognates.Port: Same spelling and meaning in German (der Port).
cognates.RAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation acronym; used untranslated in German technical writing.
cognates.RBAC: Access-control acronym; used untranslated in German technical writing.
cognates.Register: German has 'das Register' with exactly this meaning.
cognates.Register #{id}: 'Register' is the German word too; the rest is a number sign and a placeholder.
cognates.Register / Schema: Both words are the German terms; the slash is punctuation.
cognates.Repository: Established loan; the standard German term for a code repository.
cognates.Schema: Same spelling and meaning in German (das Schema).
cognates.Schemas: German admits both 'Schemas' and 'Schemata'; this bundle already uses 'Schemas'.
cognates.Score: Established loan in German analytics language (der Score).
cognates.Shards: Search-index term; German technical writing keeps 'Shards'.
cognates.Slug: URL-slug term, kept untranslated in German CMS and API tooling.
cognates.Status: Same spelling and meaning in German (der Status).
cognates.UUID:: Acronym plus a colon; German puts no space before a colon.
cognates.Version: Same spelling and meaning in German (die Version).
cognates.Webhook: Established loan; the standard term in German technical UI language.
cognates.Webhooks: Established loan; the German plural is also 'Webhooks'.
cognates.Workflows: Established loan; the German plural is also 'Workflows'.
cognates.X-Custom-Header: value\nAuthorization: B: Literal example of raw HTTP headers; header names are protocol tokens.
cognates.X-Custom-Header: value\\nAuthorization:: Literal example of raw HTTP headers, with the newline written out; protocol tokens.
Literal example of an API-key prefix; not prose.
cognates.in {register}: 'in' is the same preposition in German; the remainder is a placeholder.
cognates.myapp: Literal example value for an app identifier; not prose.
cognates.objectType: object\naction: created: Literal example of a YAML/header payload; the keys are protocol tokens.
cognates.objectType: object\\naction: created: Literal example of a YAML/header payload, with the newline written out; protocol tokens.
Literal example of an API-key prefix; not prose.
Literal example of an API-key prefix; not prose.
cognates.{property} - {other}: Two placeholders and a separating dash; nothing translatable.
cognates.{title} in {register} / {schema}: Only 'in' is translatable and it is the same preposition in German.
